name: Listen Together
description:
Watch a film together, each with your own headphones. Apple's Share Audio lets two people listen to the same iPhone or iPad with two pairs of AirPods or Beats; Listen Together brings the same idea to GNOME, with any Bluetooth headsets or speakers, of any brand, mixed freely.

HOW IT WORKS
Connect two (or more) Bluetooth audio devices. A Share Audio tile appears in Quick Settings; click it and the sound plays in all of them. Click again to go back to the output you had before. The tile is only there while at least two Bluetooth audio devices are connected, and nothing is added to the top bar.

COMPARED WITH APPLE'S SHARE AUDIO
- Devices: Apple needs AirPods or Beats. Here, any Bluetooth headset or speaker works, and two different models can be paired.
- Volume: like Apple, one volume slider per listener.
- Sync: Apple keeps its own headphones in step by itself. Other brands do not tell the computer exactly how long they take to play a sound, so two different models can be slightly apart (an echo, if they are speakers in the same room). Each device therefore has a delay slider: hold the faster one back, by ear, until the two play as one. The setting is remembered per device, so it is done once per pair.
- Stopping: sharing ends by itself when a device disconnects or when you pick another output.

NOTHING TO INSTALL
No helper program, no password, no configuration file. The extension uses PipeWire's own combine-stream module, which ships with every PipeWire desktop, and removes its virtual output as soon as sharing stops. Audio keeps playing while the screen is locked, which is why the extension stays enabled on the lock screen.

LIMITS
All the devices share one Bluetooth radio: with a weak adapter or busy 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, short dropouts can happen.
